text:
maria nguyen: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — I'm proposing we split the current QuantBridge into two explicit interfaces: a compile-time QuantDescriptor (static profile + calibration metadata) and a runtime QuantNegotiator (fallbacks, hysteresis, telemetry hooks). reasoning below.
kevin choi: I like the separation. reduces coupling between compile and runtime decisions. how do you see config discovery working?
maria nguyen: two opts: 1) image-embedded QuantDescriptor (baked into artifact) for reproducibility; 2) service-side descriptors for patching/fast rollouts. runtime still queries by model_sha + slice_id.
liam o'brien: question: if descriptor is baked, how do we safely override for emergency quality fixes? hotpatch service-side sounds necessary.
maria nguyen: exactly — descriptors are primary, service-side patch layer wins if present. we log origin in telemetry: descriptor_origin = {"artifact"|"patch"}.
sophia rao: from ops POV we need a clear contract for rollout priority + TTL on patches. no indefinite service overrides. also rate-limit patch changes to avoid noisy flips.
kevin choi: agree on TTL. also propose a safe-mode field in Descriptor: "quality_lock": [0-1] that prevents downgrades past a threshold. runtime must honor it.
maria nguyen: +1. thinking fields: precision_hint (fp8/int8/4bit), cal_stats_hash, quality_lock, calibration_date, fallback_policy_name.
liam o'brien: fallback_policy: should be declarative. e.g. "fallback_policy": "graceful->fp8->int8->full-model" with hysteresis params. runtime implements state machine.
sophia rao: include operator-visible reason codes for telemetry when fallback happens. e.g. "fallback_reason": "throughput_surge" or "deg_score_regression". we need those surfaced to console.
maria nguyen: agreed. also adding a tiny negotiation protocol: runtime sends a short preflight: `{model_sha, slice_id, prompt_prefix_hash, qos_target_ms}` and gets a tuple `{precision, expected_qos_ms, telemetry_tags}`. keeps payloads tiny.
kevin choi: can we keep the preflight synchronous but very short (10ms target)? otherwise perf regressions. maybe allow async advisory updates for longer calibrations.
maria nguyen: yes — sync for immediate decision, async for bulk recalibration updates.
liam o'brien: Edge case: cached KV states compiled with one precision, then served in another — must validate cache compatibility in Descriptor (cache_compatible_with = [list]).
sophia rao: +1. add a failsafe: if cache_incompatible and cache_present -> flush or force-compatibility mode with QA alert.
kevin choi: implementation note: keep Descriptor schema v1 small (strings + ints). store in artifacts as jsonl metadata. runtime API minimal: /negotiate and /notify_telemetry.
maria nguyen: draft snippet for Descriptor (very short):
```json
{"precision_hint":"fp8","cal_stats_hash":"abc123","quality_lock":"0.9","fallback_policy":"conservative-v1","cache_compatible_with":["fp8","int8"]}
```
liam o'brien: thanks. next: migrations. we need compatibility shim to interpret older descriptors (no quality_lock). fallback to default conservative.
sophia rao: ops playbook items: 1) patch TTL 48h default, 2) alert on >3 different patches in 1h, 3) canary flag for service-side descriptors.
approvals-bot: Deployment checklist item created: quant-bridge-refactor / require 2 approvers from eng-ml + 1 from eng-sre.
maria nguyen: action items I will take: spec PR for Descriptor/Negotiator JSON schema, small runtime stub for /negotiate, telemetry events list. assigning in the PR.
kevin choi: I'll sketch the state machine for fallback_policy and hysteresis params.
liam o'brien: I'll write compatibility tests for cache scenarios.
sophia rao: I'll draft ops playbook and alert rules.
maria nguyen: cool — let's aim for a lightweight canary next week. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
